This past Sunday, I ran the NYC Half Marathon with my incredible husband, Lee Klaskow , and fellow Googlers, Adam Kornblit and Brian Windschitl ! 🏃‍♀️🏃‍♂️🏃‍♂️🏃‍♂️ It was an unforgettable experience, pushing our limits and crossing the finish line. But more importantly, we ran with purpose, raising funds for the Vanessa T. Marcotte Foundation. ❤️ Over 600 women are assaulted every day in the US, 1 in 3 women experience sexual violence in their lifetime and 60% of women have been harassed while running. The Vanessa T. Marcotte Foundation provides educational programs and mentorship opportunities to promote female empowerment and gender equality to achieve the mission of “a world where women can live free from objectification and harassment”. To date, over 4000 women have participated in self-dense training classes provided by VMF and over $1M has been raised for educational programs and organizations supporting female empowerment. Their work is essential in creating a world where women feel safe and empowered. Knowing that our efforts are contributing to this vital mission made every mile worth it. A huge shoutout to Lee, Adam, and Brian for their unwavering support and camaraderie throughout the training and the race itself. Thank you to everyone who donated and cheered us on. Your generosity and encouragement fueled our run. #NYCHalf #Run4Vanessa #VTMF
Thank you for always being by my side- even when running 13 miles:)

6 years ago, I found myself building a department from scratch, while homeschooling my 2 children, puppy barking, and husband working in the basement all hours of the day and night. I had been hired by the JCC just 2 weeks prior to step into a role that didn't exist, to build a department that didn't exist for a group of individuals that had not yet been identified so that we could better serve the needs of the community during a global pandemic. There was no roadmap. No playbook. No department to step into and grow. No comparable experiences for us to lean on to inform impossible decisions during a time of complete uncertainty. Just sheer will to make an impact. Slowly, the department of Inclusion & Diversity started to take shape- one decision after another, one commitment after another. One family after another. We built it together with unwavering support from leadership who believed in the vision, with funders that made the growth possible, and with partners who chose to walk along side us and the community we served together. Families showed up. Staff leaned in. Capacity and programs grew. And what started as an idea at a dining room table became something real and impactful. Today, inclusion at the JCC isn’t a program, it’s woven into the very fabric of everything we do. It's how we operate. What I’m most proud of isn’t just what we built- it’s how we built something impactful, together, in the middle of chaos. We didn't wait for a model to follow- we became the model. It was never about building a department, it was about building a community where everyone had a sense of belonging. And we're still building.

On this International Women’s Day, I’m reflecting on the incredible women who have shaped my life — and continue to inspire me every day. I’m fortunate to share my life with an amazing wife ( Stefani Klaskow ) — who leads with intelligence, resilience, and integrity, while also being an extraordinary mother. She somehow balances the demands of her career with unwavering support, guidance, and love at home. Our family is stronger because of her example. I’m equally proud of my teenage daughter, who continues to impress me with her discipline and drive as a student who also finds the time to volunteer for a number of worthwhile causes. She recently added “certified yoga teacher” to her list of accomplishments. Watching her develop confidence, purpose, and a desire to help others at such a young age gives me enormous optimism for the future. And today, I’m especially thinking about my mother. She was a middle school teacher by profession, but a teacher in every sense of the word. She modeled patience, compassion, work ethic, and strength — lessons that have stayed with me long after she is gone, influencing how I show up as a parent, spouse and professional. Three generations of strong, dedicated women. Different paths. One shared foundation of commitment, character, and care for others. I’m also grateful for the opportunity through Bloomberg Intelligence ’s Talking Transport podcast ( https://apple.co/3wDmjFc ) to speak with so many accomplished women across the freight transportation landscape. I recently had the opportunity to speak with Jennifer Hedrick, CAE ( Women In Trucking Association ), Judy R. McReynolds ( ArcBest ), Lorie Tekorius ( The Greenbrier Companies ) and more. Their insights, leadership and willingness to share their experiences continue to shape important conversations in the industry and reinforce how critical diverse perspectives are to driving progress. #logisticslee #logisticlee #talkingtransports #bloombergintelligence #InternationalWomensDay #IWD2026 #transportation #logistics #freight #WomenInTrucking

The past week has been busier than usual — a reminder of how quickly geopolitics can ripple through supply chains. The war in Iran has moved energy, shipping, and freight markets in real time. When roughly 20% of global oil flows through a single chokepoint, transportation professionals don’t have the luxury of ignoring the headlines. You can see some of our work on the impact to supply chains here: https://bloom.bg/4rJFLHt But beyond markets and rates, it’s important to recognize the human cost of conflict. War brings uncertainty and hardship to families around the world. My thoughts are with all those affected — and with the U.S. service members deployed overseas, along with their families, who shoulder extraordinary responsibility during moments like this. Professionally, the volatility created a great opportunity to collaborate with my Bloomberg Intelligence colleagues across defense ( Wayne Sanders ), energy ( Salih Yilmaz, CFA ), and shipping ( Kenneth Loh ) for a Talking Transports ( https://apple.co/3wDmjFc ) podcast episode assessing the broader implications for freight markets. Cross-discipline conversations and analysis highlights the power of the BI platform. Terminal subscribers can see it for themselves at BI <GO>. It also gave me the chance to share our views on Bloomberg Television and Radio with Katie Greifeld , Romaine Bostick, CFA , Paul Sweeney and Isabelle Lee — where we tied the developments in the Middle East to oil prices and shipping rates as well as the North American trucking and railroad markets. Moments like these reinforce both how interconnected global markets are — and how fragile peace can be. #logisticslee #logisticlee #talkingtransports #bloombergintelligence #SupplyChain #Freight #Energy #Shipping #Geopolitics #trucking #Iran #BloombergIntelligence #railroads
